title: A question enters the box
brief: A user types one question into a box. Before it becomes an answer it will be counted, cached, matched with knowledge, checked and routed. Find the stop where each kind of failure belongs.

blocks.md: This guide follows **one question** through an AI system. Each stop on the way is a world. At every stop something breaks or forces a choice, and you solve it by weighing options against dials such as corpus size, update rate, permission model, latency, risk and cost. You never learn one fixed scenario, because the right answer moves when a dial moves.

blocks.title: The journey of one question
blocks.alt: A question passes through model and API, latency and cache, knowledge, tools and protocols, agents and the answer. Then senses, evaluation and observability, operations and governance, and finally boss rounds.

items.symptom: The first token takes eight seconds
items.cause: Long prefill, queueing, a cold prompt cache or a long generated answer.
items.fix: Go to w02: measure time to first token, shape prompts for cache hits and stream.

items.symptom: The assistant cannot cite our own content
items.cause: The content was never ingested, was parsed badly or was split into useless chunks.
items.fix: Go to w03 to w05: ingestion, chunking, embeddings and retrieval.

items.symptom: One user sees another team's document
items.cause: Permissions are missing from the index or a cache is shared across users.
items.fix: Go to w07: security trimming, live permission checks and cache isolation.

items.symptom: An agent loops between two tools
items.cause: Vague tool descriptions or a pattern that does not match the task.
items.fix: Go to w08 and w10: tool design and agent patterns.

items.symptom: Quality dropped after a model update and nobody noticed
items.cause: No evaluation set and no traces.
items.fix: Go to w14 and w15: evals, tracing and alerts.

items.symptom: The bill doubled in a month
items.cause: Token growth, no routing, no caching and no limits.
items.fix: Go to w01, w02 and w16: token economics, routing and cost controls.

blocks.title: What interviewers listen for
blocks.md: Strong candidates say **where on the journey** a problem lives before they name a technology. A latency complaint and a leakage complaint need different questions, even when both mention the same assistant.

quiz.q: Match each symptom to the world where you would look first.

pairs.l: Answers cite old policy because new files never reach the index
Time to first token is eight seconds
A user can retrieve another tenant's document
An agent loops between two tools

quiz.explain: Each symptom has a home stop on the journey. Stale answers start at ingestion, slow first tokens belong to latency and caching, cross-tenant leaks belong to security trimming, and tool loops belong to agent design.

quiz.q: Put the regions of the journey in the order a question meets them.
items: Knowledge: ingest, chunk, retrieve, guard, secure
Agents and protocols: tools, MCP, A2A, agents
Senses and craft: multimodal inputs, evaluation, observability
Operate and govern: cost, reliability, oversight
quiz.explain: The model and its limits come first, knowledge comes next, then tools and agents act on it. Proof of quality follows, and running the system safely at scale comes last.

takeaways: One question travels through twenty worlds, and every stop forces a choice
Name where on the journey a problem lives before you name a technology
Dials, not scenarios, decide which option wins
